newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Shark believed extinct found in Malaysian river.
newsitem.headline: Shark believed extinct found in Malaysian river.

text.p: Malaysian fishermen have caught a shark thought to have been extinct, the World Conservation Union said on Thursday.
The Borneo River Shark, a freshwater variety, was caught in the Kinabatangan river in Sabah state, northern Borneo earlier this year and kept in a tank of formalin.
It was identified last month by a visiting team of scientists.
The only other preserved example, in a Viennese museum, was taken from a Borneo river some 100 years ago, the Swiss-based agency said.
Wildlife protection bodies say sharks of all species face a growing threat of extinction, mainly because of shark fishing and the active trade in sharks and shark products around the world.
